- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly (e.g., +0.7 to +0.8), model frequently lags; add 1–3 days of upward momentum to forecast, especially if event horizon is short.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows after volatility spikes; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day avg, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- In absence of clear event context, model overestimates near-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for 30-day horizon to reduce noise.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2), model often overfits to recent highs; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
